title: Remember the forcing lines, understand the rest
outcomes: Tells a forcing line (exact recall) from a flexible position (understanding) by asking whether a natural move loses a lot or many moves work
Finds the different move that each reply to a short forcing line needs
Explains why spaced review fits forcing lines best
Sorts his own repertoire into the two kinds, with a reason for each

steps.text: Preparation has two jobs. **Exact recall** is for forcing lines, where one slip loses at once: you remember the move. **Understanding** is for flexible positions, where many moves work: you know the plan and the structure. More memorised moves is not better preparation; memory spent on flexible positions is wasted. First, sort two positions.

Real games show which lines are worth the memory. On the Openings page, after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Bc4, Black plays 3...Bc5 in 21% of games at 1100-1300 (869 of 4,100). The engine prefers 4.Nxe5, yet only 29% of White players take it in that band. The line is forcing, and each reply needs its own move. Watch it once.

steps.caption: White to move after 3...Bc5. A forcing line, with a different next move in each branch.

line.say: White takes the pawn. The e5 pawn had no defender.
d4 attacks the bishop and builds the centre.
The knight takes f7 and attacks the black queen.

claims.statement: Nxe5 is the engine's first choice (depth 16).
Nxe5 wins at least a pawn along the engine's best line.
After Nxf7 the knight attacks the queen on d8.

steps.text: **Exact recall pays** where the line is forcing and you will really meet it. **Understanding pays** where several moves work. **Rule of thumb:** if you forgot the move, could you find it in a minute from principles? If yes, understand it; if no, remember it. Spaced review (the Drill page) fits exact lines best: right answers return after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32 days; a miss returns tomorrow.
**Two more to sort.** Next: one position where a natural move loses at once, and one where many moves work.

**What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** On the Openings page you can add a line to My repertoire with a one-line note; the Drill page then asks for your move in those positions. The app cannot tell you which lines are forcing: that sort is your step, on paper. Next: three silent items.

steps.prompt: Sort your own repertoire. Use the Openings page to see how often each line is reached at your rating. Write the reason for each choice, not only the verdict.
